title: The Upkeep Rebate reduces an Agent's fees for holding other Prime Agents' tokens, creating deliberate cross-holding incentives
content:
A.2.2.7 pairs two Primitives under one purpose — ensuring "that all Agents contribute to long-term ecosystem sustainability." The Ecosystem Upkeep Fee Primitive "specifies a uniform upkeep fee payable by all Prime Agents," and the Upkeep Rebate Primitive "specifies rebates that adjust those fees for Agents holding the tokens of other Prime Agents."

The second half converts a revenue mechanism into an alignment mechanism. The fee alone would simply extract value; the rebate makes the effective rate a function of how much of the ecosystem an Agent holds. Agents are paid, in fee relief, to take positions in their peers.

What that buys is mutual exposure. An Agent holding other Agents' tokens is financially harmed by their failure and helped by their success, so competitive behaviour that damages a peer becomes partly self-damaging. This is the incentive-coincidence move the Atlas favours generally — reduce the gap between what is profitable and what is aligned, rather than exhorting Agents to cooperate.

The structural risk is the mirror image: cross-holding is also correlation. An ecosystem where Agents hold each other's tokens transmits distress between them, and a fee designed to fund sustainability ends up encouraging the balance-sheet interlinkage that makes contagion possible. The rebate calculation depends on the same market-cap valuation defined in A.2.2.7.1.2, so the whole instrument is denominated in market prices on both sides.
description: Upkeep is a two-part instrument: a uniform market-cap fee plus a rebate that pays Agents to hold each other's tokens, converting a tax into an alignment mechanism.
